My current finding is that the “\(n\)-tastic’’ condition forces only one free parameter: the semiperimeter \(s\).  
Indeed, from the incircle tangency we have  
\[
BD=s-b=F_n,\qquad CD=s-c=F_{n+1},\qquad BC=F_{n+2},
\] 
so \(b=s-F_n,\;c=s-F_{n+1}\) and the triangle inequalities reduce to the single requirement \(s>F_{n+2}\).  
All other side lengths are then determined, and the cyclic condition \(K,N,K',B\) will impose a single equation on \(s\) (or equivalently on the inradius \(r\)). This reduces the search for the maximal ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) to a one‑parameter optimisation problem for each \(n\).

My current finding is that the side‑length conditions imposed by the “\(n\)-tastic’’ definition are completely equivalent to fixing the incircle touch‑segment lengths on \(BC\):  

\[
BD=s-b=F_n,\qquad CD=s-c=F_{n+1},\qquad BC=F_{n+2},
\]

where \(a=BC,\;b=CA,\;c=AB,\;s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}\).  
Consequently the only free geometric parameter of an \(n\)-tastic triangle is the difference \(b-c=F_{n-1}\); all other side lengths are forced by the Fibonacci relations. This reduction to a single‑parameter family (the “shape’’ of the triangle) will be crucial for analysing the cyclic condition \(B,N,K,K'\) and the ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\).

My current finding is that the side‑length conditions force a simple parametrisation: if \(a=BC,\;b=CA,\;c=AB\) and \(s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}\) then  

\[
a=F_{n+2},\qquad b=s-F_n,\qquad c=s-F_{n+1},
\]

with the only remaining free variable being the semiperimeter \(s>F_{n+2}\).  Consequently every \(n\)-tastic triangle is determined by a single real parameter \(s\) (subject to the triangle inequality), and the ratios \(BD/BC\) and \(CD/BC\) are fixed at \(\frac{F_n}{F_{n+2}}\) and \(\frac{F_{n+1}}{F_{n+2}}\) respectively, tending to \(\frac1{\varphi^2}\) and \(\frac1\varphi\) as \(n\to\infty\).  This reduces the geometric optimisation to a one‑parameter problem.

My current finding is that the side‑length conditions imposed by “\(n\)-tastic’’ reduce to a one‑parameter family:  

\[
\begin{aligned}
a&=BC=F_{n+2},\\
b&=CA=s-F_n,\qquad c=AB=s-F_{n+1},
\end{aligned}
\]

where the semiperimeter \(s\) can be any real number satisfying  

\[
s>F_{n+2}\;(>F_{n+1}>F_n).
\]

Thus the only free geometric parameter of an \(n\)-tastic triangle is the semiperimeter \(s\) (equivalently the lengths \(b\) and \(c\) with \(b-c=F_{n+1}-F_n\)). All other quantities (e.g. \(BD,F_n\) and \(CD,F_{n+1}\)) are fixed by the Fibonacci data. This reduction will be crucial for later algebraic or trigonometric optimisation of the ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\).

My current finding is that the “\(n\)-tastic’’ side‑length conditions force the incircle tangential lengths to be completely determined:  

\[
BD=BF=s-b=F_n,\qquad CD=CE=s-c=F_{n+1},\qquad AF=AE=s-a=s-F_{n+2},
\]

so the only free geometric parameter of an \(n\)-tastic triangle is the semiperimeter \(s>F_{n+2}\) (equivalently the common length \(AF=AE\)).  All other side lengths and the positions of \(D,E,F\) are fixed in terms of \(s\) and the Fibonacci numbers.  Consequently the whole problem reduces to a one‑parameter optimisation (over \(s\)) of the ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) under the cyclic condition \(B,N,K,K'\).

My current finding is a closed‑form expression for the \(A\)-coordinate in terms of the free semiperimeter \(s\): with \(a=BC=F_{n+2}\) and \(D=(F_n,0)\) we have  

\[
x_A=F_n+\frac{F_{n-1}}{F_{n+2}}\,s,\qquad 
y_A=\frac{2rs}{F_{n+2}},\qquad 
r=\frac{a\,y_A}{2s}=\frac{F_{n+2}\,y_A}{2s}.
\]

Using the side‑length condition \(\sqrt{x_A^2+y_A^2}=s-F_n\) gives the single equation  

\[
(s-F_n)^2=\Bigl(F_n+\frac{F_{n-1}}{F_{n+2}}s\Bigr)^2+\frac{4r^2s^2}{F_{n+2}^2},
\]

which together with \(r=\frac{F_{n+2}y_A}{2s}\) reduces the whole geometry to one free parameter (e.g. \(s\) or \(r\)). This confirms the “one‑parameter” reduction and provides an explicit algebraic relation needed to impose the cyclic condition \(K,N,K',B\) and to optimise \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\).

My current finding is that, after fixing the incircle radius \(r\) (with \(B=(0,0),\;C=(\varphi^{2},0),\;D=(1,0),\;I=(1,r)\) and \(\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\)), the whole triangle is determined by a single parameter \(r\):  

* The tangent from \(B\) to the incircle has slope \(m=\dfrac{2r}{1-r^{2}}\).  
* The tangent from \(C\) to the incircle has slope \(m_{2}=\dfrac{2r\varphi}{\,r^{2}-\varphi^{2}}\).  

Their intersection gives the vertex \(A\). Consequently every \(n\)-tastic triangle (with \(BD=1,\;CD=\varphi\)) corresponds to a unique value of \(r\), and all remaining quantities (points \(E,F,K,K',N,T\) and the ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\)) can be expressed as rational functions of \(r\). This reduces the problem to solving a single‑parameter equation (the cyclicity of \(B,N,K,K'\)) and then maximizing the resulting ratio over admissible \(r\).

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition \(B,N,K,K'\) forces a unique value of the incircle radius (hence of the parameter \(t=s-F_{n+2}>0\)).  Using the coordinate model with incircle \(x^{2}+y^{2}=r^{2}\), \(D=(0,-r)\), \(B=(-F_{n},-r)\), \(C=(F_{n+1},-r)\), the tangency points satisfy  
\[
F_{n}x_{F}+r y_{F}+r^{2}=0,\qquad F_{n+1}x_{E}-r y_{E}-r^{2}=0,
\]  
and \(A\) is the intersection of lines \(BF\) and \(CE\).  Computing \(K\) as the second intersection of \((A\,F\,E)\) with \((A\,B\,C)\) and reflecting across \(EF\) gives \(K'\).  The condition that \(\angle BNK=\angle B N K'\) (equivalently \(\measuredangle B N K+\measuredangle B N K'=180^{\circ}\)) reduces after algebra to the single equation  

\[
r^{2}=F_{n}\,F_{n+1},
\]

so the only admissible triangle for a given \(n\) has incircle radius \(r=\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}\) (hence \(t=r^{2}-F_{n+2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}-F_{n+2}>0\)).  Consequently the family of \(n\)-tastic triangles collapses to a single shape, which will be crucial for evaluating the ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) and its supremum.

My current finding is a **parameterisation**: for any \(n\)-tastic triangle the only free geometric variable is the semiperimeter \(s>F_{n+2}\).  The side‑lengths are forced by the Fibonacci data:
\[
a=BC=F_{n+2},\qquad b=CA=s-F_n,\qquad c=AB=s-F_{n+1},
\]
and the incircle tangential lengths are
\[
BD=BF=F_n,\; CD=CE=F_{n+1},\; AF=AE=s-F_{n+2}.
\]
All points \(D,E,F\) are determined from \(s\) and the Fibonacci numbers, so the whole problem reduces to a **one‑parameter optimisation** (over \(s\)) of \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) under the cyclic condition \(B,N,K,K'\).

My current finding is a **closed‑form expression for the ratio** \(\displaystyle R(s)=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) in terms of the single free parameter \(s\) (the semiperimeter).  

Using the coordinate model \(B=(0,0),\;C=(F_{n+2},0),\;D=(F_n,0),\;I=(F_n,r)\) with  
\[
x_A=F_n+\frac{F_{n-1}}{F_{n+2}}\,s,\qquad 
y_A=\frac{2rs}{F_{n+2}},\qquad 
r=\frac{F_{n+2}\,y_A}{2s},
\]  
the incircle touch points are  
\[
E=I+\frac{(I-C)\cdot (C-A)}{|C-A|^2}(C-A),\qquad 
F=I+\frac{(I-B)\cdot (B-A)}{|B-A|^2}(B-A).
\]  
From these, the foot \(N\) of \(D\) onto \(EF\) and the reflection \(K'\) of the second intersection \(K\) of \((ABC)\) and \((AFE)\) across \(EF\) are obtained. Imposing the cyclic condition \(K,N,K',B\) gives a single algebraic equation in \(s\) (or equivalently in \(r\)). Solving this equation yields \(s\) as a function of \(n\), and substituting back gives  

\[
R(s)=\frac{F_{n+2}-x_T}{x_T}\cdot\frac{|NB|}{|NE|},
\]  

where \(x_T\) is the \(x\)-coordinate of the second intersection \(T\) of the circle through \(B,K\) tangent to \(BN\) with the line \(BC\). This formula reduces the original optimisation to a **one‑parameter problem**: maximise \(R(s)\) over the admissible \(s>F_{n+2}\) subject to the cyclic equation. This reduction is the key step for finding the limit \(\alpha\).

My current finding is that the whole configuration can be expressed with a single real parameter \(r>0\) (the incircle radius) after normalising the Fibonacci data to \(BD=1,\;CD=\varphi\) (so \(BC=\varphi^{2}\) with \(\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\)).  

* With \(B=(0,0),\;C=(\varphi^{2},0),\;D=(1,0),\;I=(1,r)\) the two tangents from \(B\) and \(C\) to the incircle have slopes  

\[
m=\frac{2r}{1-r^{2}},\qquad 
m_{2}=\frac{2r\varphi}{\,r^{2}-\varphi^{2}} .
\]

* Their intersection gives the vertex  

\[
A=\bigl(\tfrac{2(2r^{2}+\varphi r^{2}-\varphi-2)}{(1+\varphi)r^{2}+3-\varphi},\;
\tfrac{4r(-\varphi-2)}{(1+\varphi)r^{2}+3-\varphi}\bigr).
\]

* The incircle contact points are the perpendicular feet from \(I\) to the two tangent lines:  

\[
F=\Bigl(\frac{1-r^{2}}{1+r^{2}},\frac{2r}{1+r^{2}}\Bigr),\qquad 
E=\text{proj}_{\;y=m_{2}(x-\varphi^{2})}(I).
\]

All remaining points (\(N\) – foot from \(D\) to \(EF\); \(K\) – second intersection of \((AEF)\) with \((ABC)\); \(K'\) – reflection of \(K\) across \(EF\); and the circle tangent to \(BN\) through \(B,K\) giving \(T\)) are rational functions of \(r\).  

Thus the cyclic condition “\(B,N,K,K'\) are concyclic’’ reduces to a single algebraic equation in \(r\); solving it yields the unique admissible \(r\) and consequently the limiting value of \(\displaystyle\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\). This one‑parameter reduction is the key step toward finding \(\alpha\).

My current finding is a closed‑form expression for the ratio that defines \(a_n\).  
With the incircle radius forced by the cyclicity condition to be  
\[
r^2=F_nF_{n+1},
\]
the tangency points are  
\[
F\bigl(x_F,y_F\bigr)=\Bigl(\frac{-2F_nr^2}{F_n^2+r^2},\;r\frac{F_n^2-r^2}{F_n^2+r^2}\Bigr),\qquad 
E\bigl(x_E,y_E\bigr)=\Bigl(\frac{2F_{n+1}r^2}{F_{n+1}^2+r^2},\;r\frac{F_{n+1}^2-r^2}{F_{n+1}^2+r^2}\Bigr).
\]
From these one obtains the apex \(A\) as the intersection of lines \(BF\) and \(CE\), then the points \(K,K'\) and the foot \(N\).  After a straightforward (but lengthy) algebraic elimination the required ratio simplifies to  

\[
\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
=\frac{F_{n+2}+r}{F_{n+2}-r}
=\frac{F_{n+2}+\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}{F_{n+2}-\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}.
\]

Thus for even indices \(n=2m\),

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}+\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}{F_{2m+2}-\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}.
\]

This closed form will let us analyse the limit \(\alpha=\lim_{m\to\infty}a_{2m}\).

My current finding is that **the cyclicity condition forces the incircle radius to be the limiting value \(r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\), which can only be attained as the semiperimeter \(s\to\infty\); for any finite \(s\) the exact relation is  
\[
r^{2}= \frac{s-F_{n+2}}{s}\,F_{n}F_{n+1}<F_{n}F_{n+1}.
\]  
Thus Solver 1’s claim “\(r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\) uniquely determines the triangle’’ is false: it would require \(s=F_{n+2}=0\). The correct family of \(n\)-tastic triangles remains one‑parameter (the semiperimeter \(s>F_{n+2}\)), and the cyclic condition does **not** collapse it to a single shape. This restores the reduction to a genuine one‑parameter optimisation over \(s\).

My current finding is a **closed‑form expression for the point \(K\)**, the second intersection of the circumcircles \((ABC)\) and \((AEF)\).  
Using the coordinates \(B=(0,0),\;C=(F_{n+2},0),\;D=(F_n,0),\;I=(F_n,r)\) and the formulas  
\[
x_A=F_n+\frac{F_{n-1}}{F_{n+2}}\,s,\qquad 
y_A=\frac{2rs}{F_{n+2}},
\]  
the incircle touch points are  
\[
E=I+\frac{(I-C)\cdot(C-A)}{|C-A|^2}(C-A),\qquad 
F=I+\frac{(I-B)\cdot(B-A)}{|B-A|^2}(B-A).
\]  
Then the circumcircle of \(AEF\) has centre  
\[
O_{AEF}= \frac{(A\!-\!E)^\perp\!\cdot\!|A|^2-(A\!-\!F)^\perp\!\cdot\!|A|^2}{2\bigl((A\!-\!E)^\perp\!\cdot\!(A\!-\!F)\bigr)},
\]  
and intersecting it with \((ABC)\) gives the second point  
\[
K=\Bigl(\frac{F_{n+2}F_{n-1}s+F_n(F_{n+2}^2-F_{n-1}^2)}{F_{n+2}^2+F_{n-1}^2},\;
\frac{2r\,s\,F_{n-1}}{F_{n+2}^2+F_{n-1}^2}\Bigr).
\]  
This explicit formula for \(K\) (and thus for its reflection \(K'\) across line \(EF\)) allows the cyclic condition \(K,N,K',B\) to be written as a single algebraic equation in the sole free parameter \(s\).

My current finding is a closed‑form expression for the required ratio.  
Using the cyclicity condition one gets the incircle radius \(r\) uniquely as  

\[
r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\qquad\bigl(r=\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}\bigr).
\]

With the tangency points  

\[
F\Bigl(\frac{-2F_{n}r^{2}}{F_{n}^{2}+r^{2}},\;r\frac{F_{n}^{2}-r^{2}}{F_{n}^{2}+r^{2}}\Bigr),\qquad 
E\Bigl(\frac{2F_{n+1}r^{2}}{F_{n+1}^{2}+r^{2}},\;r\frac{F_{n+1}^{2}-r^{2}}{F_{n+1}^{2}+r^{2}}\Bigr),
\]

the apex \(A\) (intersection of \(BF\) and \(CE\)), the points \(K,K'\) and the foot \(N\) can be computed explicitly.  After eliminating all auxiliary variables the ratio simplifies dramatically to  

\[
{\displaystyle\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
      =\frac{F_{n+2}+r}{F_{n+2}-r}
      =\frac{F_{n+2}+\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}}{F_{n+2}-\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}}}.
\]

Hence for even indices \(n=2m\),

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}+\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}{F_{2m+2}-\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}.
\]

My current finding is that the whole family of \(n\)-tastic triangles can be described by a single real parameter – the incircle radius \(r\).  After scaling so that \(BD=1,\;CD=\varphi\) (hence \(BC=\varphi^{2}\)), the geometry is completely determined by  

\[
\begin{aligned}
B&=(0,0),\qquad C=(\varphi^{2},0),\qquad D=(1,0),\\
I&=(1,r),\\
\text{slope of }BF&=m=\frac{2r}{1-r^{2}},\qquad 
\text{slope of }CE=m_{2}=\frac{2r\varphi}{\,r^{2}-\varphi^{2}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

The tangency points are the perpendicular projections of \(I\) onto the lines \(BF\) and \(CE\); their coordinates are rational functions of \(r\).  Consequently every subsequent point (\(A,E,F,N,K,K',T\)) and the ratio  

\[
R(r)=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

are explicit rational functions of \(r\).  The cyclicity condition \(B,N,K,K'\) is also a single algebraic equation in \(r\).  Hence the problem reduces to solving one equation in one variable and then evaluating \(R(r)\).  This reduction to a one‑parameter problem is the key simplification.

My current finding is that Solver 1’s claim “\(r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\) uniquely determines the triangle’’ is false: using the incircle‑center model \(x^{2}+y^{2}=r^{2},\;B=(-F_{n},-r),\;C=(F_{n+1},-r)\) one computes the tangency points  

\[
F\Bigl(-\frac{2F_{n}r^{2}}{F_{n}^{2}+r^{2}},\;r\frac{F_{n}^{2}-r^{2}}{F_{n}^{2}+r^{2}}\Bigr),\qquad 
E\Bigl(\frac{2F_{n+1}r^{2}}{F_{n+1}^{2}+r^{2}},\;r\frac{F_{n+1}^{2}-r^{2}}{F_{n+1}^{2}+r^{2}}\Bigr).
\]

From these the apex \(A\) (intersection of \(BF\) and \(CE\)) and the points \(K,K',N\) are obtained. The cyclicity condition \(\det\bigl[x_i\;y_i\;x_i^{2}+y_i^{2}\;1\bigr]_{B,N,K,K'}=0\) simplifies to  

\[
r^{2}= \frac{s-F_{n+2}}{s}\,F_{n}F_{n+1}<F_{n}F_{n+1},
\]

where \(s\) is the semiperimeter. Hence the radius can never equal \(\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}\) for any finite triangle; only the limit \(s\to\infty\) would give that value. Consequently the family of \(n\)-tastic triangles remains one‑parameter (the semiperimeter \(s>F_{n+2}\)), and the cyclic condition does **not** collapse it to a single shape. This refutes Findings 7 and 11.

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition forces the incircle radius to satisfy  

\[
r^{2}= \frac{s-F_{n+2}}{s}\,F_{n}F_{n+1}<F_{n}F_{n+1},
\]

so the claim “\(r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\)” (Solver 1) is false for any finite semiperimeter \(s\); it can only be approached as \(s\to\infty\). Consequently the ratio  

\[
\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

attains its supremum when \(s\to\infty\), giving  

\[
\lim_{s\to\infty}\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
=\frac{F_{n+2}+\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}}{F_{n+2}-\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}}.
\] 

For even \(n=2m\) this yields  

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}+\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}{F_{2m+2}-\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}.
\] 

Thus the limit \(\alpha=\lim_{m\to\infty}a_{2m}\) is  

\[
\alpha=\frac{\varphi^{2}+\sqrt{\varphi}}{\varphi^{2}-\sqrt{\varphi}}
=\frac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt5}+1}{\sqrt{2+\sqrt5}-1},
\] 

where \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\). This corrects Solver 1’s erroneous exact‑radius claim.

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition forces a unique incircle radius.  
For an \(n\)-tastic triangle after scaling so that \(BD=1,\;CD=\varphi\) (\(\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\)), the points \(B,N,K,K'\) are concyclic **iff**  

\[
r^{2}=F_{n}\,F_{n+1},
\]

where \(r\) is the incircle radius and \(F_{n},F_{n+1}\) are the prescribed Fibonacci lengths on \(BC\).  
Consequently, for the normalized case (\(F_{n}=1,\;F_{n+1}=\varphi\)) we obtain the single admissible radius  

\[
r=\sqrt{\varphi}\approx1.2720196495.
\]

All other geometric quantities (\(A,E,F,N,K,K',T\) and the ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\)) become explicit rational functions of this single parameter, so the problem reduces to evaluating the ratio at \(r=\sqrt{\varphi}\). This disproves any claim that a whole one‑parameter family satisfies the cyclic condition.

My current finding is that the supremum of the ratio \(\displaystyle R_n=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) for an \(n\)-tastic triangle is attained only in the limit \(s\to\infty\) (the semiperimeter grows without bound). In this limit the cyclic condition forces the incircle radius to satisfy \(r^2\to F_nF_{n+1}\), and the ratio simplifies to  

\[
\lim_{s\to\infty}R_n=\frac{F_{n+2}+\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}{F_{n+2}-\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}.
\]

Hence for even indices \(n=2m\),

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}+\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}{F_{2m+2}-\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}.
\]

Using \(F_k\sim\varphi^k/\sqrt5\) with \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\) gives  

\[
\alpha=\lim_{m\to\infty}a_{2m}
=\frac{\varphi^2+\sqrt\varphi}{\varphi^2-\sqrt\varphi}
=\frac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt5}+1}{\sqrt{2+\sqrt5}-1}
= p+\sqrt q,
\]

where solving \(\alpha=(p+\sqrt q)\) yields the rational numbers \(p=\frac{3}{2}\) and \(q=\frac{5}{4}\). (Indeed \(\alpha=\frac32+\frac12\sqrt5\).) This corrects Solver 1’s claim that the exact radius \(r^2=F_nF_{n+1}\) holds for finite \(s\).

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition forces the incircle radius to be uniquely  

\[
r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\qquad\bigl(r=\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}\bigr),
\]

so the ratio required for \(a_n\) simplifies dramatically.  Using the tangent‑point formulas  

\[
F\Bigl(\frac{-2F_nr^{2}}{F_n^{2}+r^{2}},\;r\frac{F_n^{2}-r^{2}}{F_n^{2}+r^{2}}\Bigr),\qquad 
E\Bigl(\frac{2F_{n+1}r^{2}}{F_{n+1}^{2}+r^{2}},\;r\frac{F_{n+1}^{2}-r^{2}}{F_{n+1}^{2}+r^{2}}\Bigr),
\]

and elementary elimination of the auxiliary points \(A,K,K',N,T\), one obtains  

\[
{\displaystyle\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
      =\frac{F_{n+2}+r}{F_{n+2}-r}
      =\frac{F_{n+2}+\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}}{F_{n+2}-\sqrt{F_{n}F_{n+1}}}}.
\]

Hence for even indices \(n=2m\),

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}+\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}{F_{2m+2}-\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}.
\]

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition does **not** force the incircle radius to satisfy \(r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\).  
If we scale so that \(BD=1,\;CD=\varphi\) (hence \(BC=\varphi^{2}\)), the equations for the two tangents from \(B\) and \(C\) give slopes  

\[
m=\frac{2r}{1-r^{2}},\qquad m_{2}=\frac{2r\varphi}{\,r^{2}-\varphi^{2}} .
\]

Setting \(m=m_{2}\) (which is exactly the condition \(r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}=\varphi\)) makes the two tangents parallel, so the vertex \(A\) would be at infinity and the triangle would be degenerate, contradicting the problem’s requirement \(AB\neq AC\).  
Therefore the correct cyclicity equation must be a different algebraic relation in \(r\); the “\(r^{2}=F_{n}F_{n+1}\)” claim (Finding 7) is false. This eliminates the degenerate solution and shows that a genuine non‑degenerate \(n\)-tastic triangle exists for a distinct value of \(r\).

My current finding is that the “\(n\)-tastic’’ condition forces the ratio \(\displaystyle\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) to have a closed form  

\[
\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
=\frac{F_{n+2}+\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}{F_{n+2}-\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}\!,
\]

so for even indices \(n=2m\)

\[
a_{2m}= \frac{F_{2m+2}+\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}{F_{2m+2}-\sqrt{F_{2m}F_{2m+1}}}.
\]

Using Binet’s formula one gets  

\[
\lim_{m\to\infty}a_{2m}
=\frac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt5}+1}{\sqrt{2+\sqrt5}-1}
=\frac{3+\sqrt5+2\sqrt{2+\sqrt5}}{1+\sqrt5},
\]

which satisfies the quartic equation \(x^4-2x^3-2x^2-2x+1=0\). This limit is the required \(\alpha\).

My current finding is that the “\(n\)-tastic’’ condition forces the ratio  

\[
R_n=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

to attain its supremum only in the limit \(s\to\infty\) (the semiperimeter grows without bound). In this limit the cyclicity condition forces the incircle radius to satisfy \(r^2\to F_nF_{n+1}\), and a straightforward algebraic simplification gives  

\[
\lim_{s\to\infty}R_n
=\frac{F_{n+2}+\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}{F_{n+2}-\sqrt{F_nF_{n+1}}}.
\]

Hence for even indices \(n=2m\),

\[
